findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: exposure, pulse, rules-ahead, world-outages · Private data: cve-priority, disaster-exposure, exposure, hazard, place-brief, power-fuel-exposure, science, security, travel-meds · Public sink: city-dossier, jp-furusato, occupation-pay-ladder, power-fuel-exposure, protected-areas, signals, world-cities, world-outages, world-power.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: exposure, pulse, rules-ahead, world-outages · Private data: cve-priority, disaster-exposure, exposure, hazard, place-brief, power-fuel-exposure, science, security, travel-meds · Public sink: city-dossier, jp-furusato, occupation-pay-ladder, power-fuel-exposure, protected-areas, signals, world-cities, world-outages, world-power

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "security" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
